1 تَلِفَ , (S, M, Msb, K,) aor.
تَلَفَ , (K,) inf. n. تَلَفٌ, (Lth, T, S, M, &c.,) He, or it, (a thing, Lth, T, S, Msb, of any kind, Lth, T,) perished, passed away, was not, was no more, became nonexistent or annihilated; or went away, no one knew whither; or became in a bad, or corrupt, state; became corrupted, vitiated, marred, or spoiled; [in this sense the verb is often used in the present
day;] or he died: syn. هَلَكَ; (M, K;) and of the inf. n., عَطَبٌ (Lth, T,) and هَلَاكٌ. (Lth, T, S.) [See also تَلَفٌ, below.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
